summary: A 1927 D-5 ground cab still stands beside the 50-ft octagonal-cab tower finished in 2001 on Calamity Butte, a staffed Malheur National Forest lookout in Harney County.

facts.design: 50-ft pole tower with octagonal cab (completed 2001); the original 1927 D-5 ground cab is still on site

access.note: Still an active Forest Service lookout; the sources reviewed give no visitor rules. Check with the Malheur National Forest before visiting.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Malheur historical notes quoted by Forest Lookouts say the 1927 lookout house was built on Bald Butte and the point was later renamed Calamity Butte; Every Lookout in Oregon describes the 1927 cabin as built on Calamity Butte. The later name is the same point.

notes_for_editor: Design labels conflict and are not resolved: D-5 ground house (Forest Lookouts, Every Lookout in Oregon), Region-5 cab (firelookout.com), 14x14 'Supervisor Hall Special' on a revised California design (register). The register page dates from the 1994 registration and describes the ground cab as the lookout, which predates the 2001 tower. Elevation: register 6,666 ft (record's 2,031.8 m matches), firelookout.com and Every Lookout in Oregon 6,695 ft. Staffing 'every summer' on firelookout.com is undated; the dated record is the July 2021 visit. No rental listing found in the FFLA rentals page or the sources read. Access: a rough forest road to an active Forest Service lookout; no visitor rules in sources, so access level is public with a check-first note. Record kind 'tower' and height 15.2 m match the 2001 tower, so no correction proposed. Story edit 2026-10-08: the 1927 cab's presence on the summit is cited to firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts and Every Lookout, not to the register, which does not date its cab; the staffing sentence is limited to what the sources date.
